subject: dracula ant
title: The Fastest Known Animal Movement Is an Ant's Jaw Snap: 200 mph

scenes.text: The fastest thing any animal does, you can't even see.
It belongs to the Dracula ant, a small ant that lives in the leaf litter of Borneo.
It presses the tips of its jaws together until one slips past the other, like snapping your fingers.
The jaw hits ninety meters a second, over two hundred miles an hour, in as little as 23 millionths of a second.
About five thousand times faster than a blink.
It smacks prey into tunnel walls with it. The name? Adults sip blood from the colony's larvae.

description:
The fastest animal movement ever measured is the jaw snap of the Dracula ant, Mystrium camillae: up to 90 metres per second, more than 200 miles an hour.
The ant presses its mandible tips together until one slides across the other, like a finger snap; a strike can be over in as little as 23 microseconds, about 5,000 times faster than a blink (Royal Society Open Science, December 2018). The ants studied came from Sabah, on Borneo. They are called Dracula ants because adults feed on the blood of larvae without killing them.
What is the fastest thing you have ever seen an animal do? Comment below.
first_comment: The snap is about 1,000 times faster than your own finger snap, and the ant loads it for up to 3.7 seconds first. What should we clock next?
